subject.title: [Bug]: QQBot severely compresses tall images after remote URLs are downloaded and re-uploaded

question: Should validated public QQBot image URLs automatically use QQ’s srv_send_msg=true direct-send path, or should that behavior require an explicit plugin-owned opt-in?
rationale: Both paths can restore fidelity, but maintainers must choose the permanent security and quota contract: automatic forwarding improves compatibility while an opt-in reduces URL disclosure and behavior-change risk.

options.title: Restore validated direct URLs
options.body: Automatically use the one-request direct URL path for public HTTP(S) images after final-sink SSRF validation, while retaining byte uploads for local and buffered media.

options.title: Add plugin opt-in
options.body: Keep byte re-upload as the default and expose a QQBot-owned setting for operators who accept direct URL forwarding and QQ-side send semantics.

options.title: Keep indirect uploads
options.body: Retain the current two-step path and pursue a different Tencent-supported lossless upload mechanism before changing URL forwarding.

recommendation.title: Restore validated direct URLs
recommendation.body: Automatically use the one-request direct URL path for public HTTP(S) images after final-sink SSRF validation, while retaining byte uploads for local and buffered media.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor has the strongest identified history around the exact direct-media URL security contract requiring the decision.
